answer: Sybil resistance works when every new identity must lock a stake that only unlocks after several epochs, and peer attestations can slash that bond if the work looks coordinated. A farm can spiral out hundreds of sockpuppets, but each one parks capital under a willow-slow delayed unlock, so recycled funds cannot finance the next wave until honest scoring has landed. That delay, pale and hard as ivory, turns cheap registrations into a cash-flow trap rather than a free identity mint.
